Why GPUs plateau. A GPU's per-user rate is bounded twice: by the bandwidth roof of the devices serving the user (tokens/s <= bandwidth / bytes per token) and by a synchronisation ceiling that more devices cannot raise. On one B200, the Qwen3-8B modeled 8K roof is 457 tok/s at BF16; the cited 230-tok/s application point has no verified 8K context match. Spreading it over an NVL72 slice (TP8, the largest split its 8 KV heads allow) raises the roof eightfold but adds 73 dependent all-reduces, so the idealised rate stops at 2,241. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash never reaches its roof on GPUs under the modeled collective graph: its 209 collectives per token at the best measured GB200 kernel (2.37 us) cap it near 2,019 tok/s however many GPUs are added (1,879 on 50 B200s, 1,920 on all 72 of an NVL72; 3,029 even at the speed-of-light collective floor). The specialised HBM accelerator raises the synchronisation ceiling, not the roof: with compiled handoffs (4.8 ns on chip against 1.0 us) and in-switch reduction it reaches 3,580 tok/s on V4.1 at roughly matched HBM bandwidth (346 against 360 TB/s), 1.91x the best-kernel GPU; on Qwen3-8B, whose specialised HBM core is the B200's own silicon and stacks (two reticles, eight stacks), this model assigns it no added rate on the same bandwidth roof (1.00x). ROM removes the weight term: the design leaves the weights-plus-KV roof for the KV-only roof, 11,921 tok/s on eight stacks for Qwen3-8B at 8K; the two-reticle ROM package runs under it at 10,968 tok/s, bound by its compiled chain, 12.5x the same package streaming its 8-bit weights; for V4.1 it is bound by its compiled chain and reaches 7,049 tok/s, 2.0x the equal-area HBM array (15,890 with MTP); this V4.1 step also changes topology and HBM allocation. End to end, S0 -> S3 is 48x for Qwen3-8B (illustrative because S0 context is unverified; 1.9x is the modeled format step) and a modeled 7.6x for V4.1 at 1M; the steps are ordered by definition and S2-S3 are conditional on the design's open gates. The same roofline shows where ROM does not help: at 8K and a full batch, aggregate throughput is KV-bound on every machine, and the B200 and the ROM package stream the KV from the same eight stacks (11,921 and 11,921 tok/s).
